title: RTX 5090 engine keep-warm: --gpu-keep-warm-ms holds P1 at about 100 W, new sessions after 12-58 s idle start at back-to-back speed, and outputs stay byte-identical
question: Built into ninfer-serve, does a grace-period keep-warm hold the RTX 5090 in P1 after requests, bring new sessions after idle back to back-to-back latency, keep every output byte, and cost nothing on requests that arrive while it runs? What grace does production's traffic need, at what power?
answer: Yes. With ninfer-serve --gpu-keep-warm-ms N (off by default), the Engine worker keeps the GPU warm once it has run work and gone idle: a single-warp kernel spins 3.5 ms of every 10 ms on its own stream until a request is pending, the Engine stops, or N ms pass. With production's arguments on the RTX 5090 it held P1 (SM 2,670-2,700 MHz, memory 13,801 MHz, 35% utilization) at 99.5-102.7 W. Idle in P8 draws 29.3-29.8 W, so the hold costs about 71 W. New sessions after 12, 25, 38, 53 and 58 s of idle prefilled in 0.155-0.157 s (TTFT 0.173-0.181 s), the same as back to back (0.156-0.160 s). With it off they took 0.253-0.304 s (TTFT 0.316-0.366 s). Holds up to 58 s did not slow the next session, as EXP-061's side-process load had after 60 s. When the 30 s grace ended the card reached P8 2.9 s later, and the session at 45 s was cold again (0.352 s). All 89 role-corpus cases were byte-identical to production v0.8.1 with it on and with it off. 80 corpus requests arrived 1-5 ms after the previous response, while the spin launched at idle could still be running. They lost nothing measurable: paired TTFT median -0.1 ms, worst +4.4 ms. In production's v0.7.0 traffic, agent requests that arrived after 5 s or more of idle had waited a median 52.7 s. A 30 s grace would have caught 11 of 138 of them. 60 s would have caught 84 (74 of 103 new sessions), holding the card for 3.2% of the logged 62 h, about 2.29 W on average.
decision: Open, prototype only. The change is on a local runtime branch and nothing is released. It was measured at c6bd1674; head 0e996b3d adds a one-spin-in-flight guard, which was built and host-tested but not run on the GPU. Production stays on v0.8.1. Adopting it takes a runtime release with the flag and a deployment argument. Production's idle times point to a 60 s grace: it covers 84 of 138 idle arrivals and adds about 2.3 W on average. That call is the founder's.

method.change: ninfer-serve --gpu-keep-warm-ms N sets EngineOptions::gpu_keep_warm_ms, and server_start records it. The Engine worker waits for work once nothing is pending, materializing or active. If it has run work since it last went idle, it calls GpuKeepWarm::launch() every 10 ms. Each call starts one single-warp %globaltimer spin of 3.5 ms on a non-blocking stream owned by the worker thread. It stops when a request is pending, the Engine stops, or N ms pass, then waits without a timeout. Nothing on the request path synchronizes with that stream. The default is 0 (off).
method.build: Release, sm_120a, GNU 13.3.0 and nvcc 13.1.115 (production's toolchain). The serve-options and request-log host tests pass. The binary is mounted into production's v0.8.1 image in place of its ninfer-serve.
method.window_1: 2026-09-26 14:09-14:31Z: production held and stopped. The candidate served on a side port with production's arguments and seccomp profile, first with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 30000 and then with 0. Each arm sent one cold request whose ~30K-token system message and 12 tool definitions form the stable prefix, then six new two-message sessions after 0, 12, 0, 25, 0 and 45 s. nvidia-smi sampled P-state, clocks, power and utilization every 50 ms. Each arm then ran the 89-case role corpus (84 requests), compared byte for byte with production v0.8.1's run. Production was restored healthy.
method.window_2: 14:37-14:42Z: the same with --gpu-keep-warm-ms 60000 only and no corpus. Sessions came after 0, 38, 0, 53, 0 and 58 s: production's first quartile and median idle before an idle arrival, then the end of the grace. Production was restored healthy.
method.analysis: Per idle gap: the P-state at send and the first appearance of each P-state after the previous response. P-state counts, median power and median clocks are taken from 2 s after the response to the end of the grace, or to 0.1 s before the next request if sooner; after the grace, from 10 s past its end. Corpus requests are paired in order between arms; all 84 pairs have the same prompt, computed and completion tokens. The idle before a request is its server start less the previous request's finish.
method.coverage: Production's v0.7.0 request logs (EXP-060's source): for each grace G, the agent requests that arrived after 5 s or more of idle but within G, and min(gap, G) summed over every idle gap. The energy uses the measured power above idle.

candidate_head.source: 0e996b3d (c6bd1674 plus a guard that skips a launch while the previous spin still runs)

sources.gpu: RTX 5090, Windows driver 610.88, CUDA through WSL2 and Docker Desktop

limits: One card and driver (610.88) over two windows, with one new session per gap length per arm.
The engine ran one load shape only: 3.5 ms of every 10 ms. EXP-061 measured the holding threshold (30% holds, 25% does not) at a 100 ms period.

Head 0e996b3d adds a guard: a launch is skipped while the previous spin still runs, and cudaErrorNotReady is cleared from the thread's last error, as PyTorch's CUDAStream::query does. The Engine checks the last error after its own launches. The guard was built and host-tested but not run on the GPU. On a GPU that the Engine has to itself, each 3.5 ms spin ends 6.5 ms before the next launch, so the guard should never skip there (inferred, not observed).

The first ten back-to-back corpus requests after the runner's start-up (7.8 s idle with it off) were 5.2-13.3 ms faster with it on. The other 70 differ by -3.5 to +4.4 ms. The clock ramp after idle may outlast one request; this was not traced.

Power is the board sensor as nvidia-smi reports it, sampled every 50 ms. The average-power estimate multiplies the held seconds by the measured power above idle and ignores the 1-3 s step-down after each grace.

Coverage uses v0.7.0 traffic and assumes the grace restarts after every request. It counts arrivals, not seconds saved. EXP-060 put production's new sessions after idle at 0.361 s TTFT, against 0.199 s near back to back.

The RTX 4090 and RTX 3090 lanes were not built or measured, and their idle P-states are unmeasured. Concurrency above 1 was not measured; the idle condition (nothing pending, materializing or active) is the same.
